item.title: Chi Phi Members Accused in Cornell Sex Assault Lawsuit Give Varying Accounts of Night
item.description: Their accounts, detailed in hundreds of pages of investigative files obtained by The New York Times, were disjointed and sometimes contradictory. All the men denied any wrongdoing.
item.dc:creator: Maia Coleman, Claire Fahy and Michael C. Bender
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: At the Chi Phi fraternity house at Cornell University, a student identified as Jane Doe said she was raped multiple times in October 2024.

item.title: Cornell Students Question Greek Life Culture After Sexual Assault Claim
item.description: With their university under fire in the wake of a sexual assault lawsuit, students are having difficult conversations about Greek life, campus rituals and the possibility for lasting changes.
item.dc:creator: Emma Goldberg
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Media outlets have descended on the Cornell campus in recent days after the district attorney announced he is reopening the investigation into a 2024 sexual assault case.

item.title: Cornell Will Hire Outside Lawyers to Investigate 2024 Rape Claim
item.description: The university and law enforcement officials are under growing pressure to explain how they handled a woman’s initial claims of being assaulted by a group of students.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Maag
item.media:credit: Victor J. Blue for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gov. Kathy Hochul said that parents should be able to feel confident that their children are safe when attending college.

item.title: E.E.O.C. Sues Harvard for Data on Diversity in Hiring Practices
item.description: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission filed a lawsuit asking a judge to compel the university to provide information on hiring practices that the agency said discriminated against white men.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Davis O’Brien and Michael C. Bender
item.media:credit: Sophie Park for The New York Times
item.media:description: Harvard has been a frequent target of federal officials under the Trump administration.

item.title: Hundreds Detained in France as Some Student Protests Turn Violent
item.description: French high schoolers are protesting teacher shortages and overcrowded classrooms, in France’s latest flare-up over education and public services.
item.dc:creator: Amelia Nierenberg
item.media:credit: Abdul Saboor/Reuters

item.title: Students at Cornell Daily Sun Pursued Sexual Assault Case for Two Years
item.description: The student newspaper, The Cornell Daily Sun, covered the allegations of rape at a fraternity house since they were first made in 2024 and led the reporting on the case.
item.dc:creator: Emma Goldberg
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Cornell Daily Sun is independent of the university and has its offices off campus.

item.title: A Timeline of the Cornell University Rape Investigation
item.description: Prosecutors have reopened an inquiry into a former student’s claims that several men sexually assaulted her in a campus fraternity house.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Barnes
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Cornell University administrators and the Tompkins County district attorney are under pressure over their handling of a former student’s allegations.

item.title: Dartmouth Provost Is the Latest College Professor Examined for A.I. Use
item.description: Dartmouth said it would investigate its provost over A.I. accusations. Similar controversies on other campuses have prompted frustration among students.
item.dc:creator: Mark Arsenault and Alan Blinder
item.media:credit: Caleb Kenna for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dartmouth College’s president has encouraged A.I., but now the school is investigating how one of its professors used A.I.

item.title: MacArthur Foundation Announces 2026 ‘Genius Grant’ Winners
item.description: The 20 fellowship recipients across the arts, humanities and sciences will each receive an $800,000, no-strings-attached stipend for their work.

item.title: Cornell’s Chi Phi Chapter Faces Scrutiny Over Assault Accusations
item.description: Chi Phi’s Cornell chapter was shuttered after a woman said its members sexually assaulted her. It was one of the oldest fraternities at the school, where Greek life has thrived.
item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder and Michael S. Schmidt
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Chi Phi fraternity house at Cornell University.

item.title: University of Michigan Halts New Grading Plan After Backlash From Critics
item.description: The program was intended to address what the university called a “mental health crisis.” But the plan was met with criticism that it was coddling students.
item.dc:creator: Madaleine Rubin
item.media:credit: Sylvia Jarrus for The New York Times
item.media:description: The University of Michigan campus in Ann Arbor.

item.title: As Mr. Belding on “Saved by the Bell,” Dennis Haskins Made Principals Your Pal

item.title: College Students Flex Their Power in A.I. Investment Frenzy
item.description: Dorm Room Fund, a program that lets college students invest in their peers, raised a new $50 million fund as the competition for young founders ramps up.
item.dc:creator: Erin Griffith

item.media:description: Molly Fowler, a partner at Dorm Room Fund, at her office in Manhattan. The venture capital firm has raised a new $50 million fund.

item.title: U.S. News Shuffled Its N.Y. High School Rankings. An Uproar Ensued.

item.media:description: Robert Kravitz, superintendent of Jericho Union Free School District on Long Island, was upset when his school’s rating plummeted.

item.title: Where Things Stand in the Jane Doe Investigation
item.description: Gov. Kathy Hochul has named a special investigator, Letitia James, as the allegations of rape in a fraternity house become part of a national conversation about sexual assault and consent.

item.title: Tariffs Are Making Instruments So Expensive, School Music Programs Are at Risk
item.description: When a single cello can cost $1,000 and a tuba $9,000, tariffs are straining meager band and orchestra budgets.
item.dc:creator: Sydney Ember and Maddie McGarvey
item.media:description: Many schools rely on inexpensive beginner instruments that are made largely in China.

item.title: Why Prosecutors May Face Legal Hurdles in the Cornell Investigation
item.description: Experts in sexual assault cases said it may not be easy to win a conviction on the rape allegations that Jane Doe has made against fraternity members.
item.dc:creator: Santul Nerkar and Benjamin Weiser
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Cornell University has been rocked by accusations that seven male students sexually assaulted a woman.

item.title: N.Y. Lawmakers and Victims Push to Change Rape Law in Intoxication Cases
item.description: Accusations that Cornell University students assaulted a woman while she was impaired have renewed calls to amend the law.
item.dc:creator: Maria Cramer
item.media:credit: Maria Cramer/The New York Times
item.media:description: Legislators, assault survivors and activists called on Thursday to change New York’s rape law in cases in which victims were intoxicated.

item.title: Hochul Names Letitia James as Special Prosecutor in Cornell Case
item.description: Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed the state attorney general to investigate a former Cornell University student’s allegation of rape. The woman has sued seven men in connection with the alleged assault.
item.dc:creator: Santul Nerkar, Benjamin Oreskes and Hurubie Meko
item.media:credit: Ryan Murphy for The New York Times
item.media:description: Letitia James, the state attorney general, had already begun to review the way law enforcement handled the Cornell University assault allegation.

item.title: Cornell Students Call for Change at Fiery Public Meeting
item.description: Through tears, some students shared stories of assaults they had experienced, while others spoke out to criticize administrators and demand improved training on consent.
item.dc:creator: Emma Goldberg
item.media:credit: Emma Goldberg/The New York Times
item.media:description: At a public forum at Cornell’s student union, some students expressed rage at the way a rape allegation was handled.

item.title: Cornell Documents Raise Questions About Handling of Rape Allegations

item.title: Anger and Questions at Cornell
item.description: Readers discuss the allegations of sexual assault at Cornell University. Also: A botched execution, and a pause, in Tennessee.
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times

item.title: As Cornell Reckons with Sexual Assault Case, Will Applicants Think Twice?
